news.download-pdf.content: From the view page, click the new PDF button in the toolbar (next to the print button) to generate and download a PDF of your sequence, ready to share or archive.
news.download-pdf.step1.alt: View page toolbar with the new PDF button highlighted
news.download-pdf.step1.description: In the top toolbar of the view page you will find the new PDF button (document icon) next to the orientation and print buttons. Click it to start the download.
news.download-pdf.step2.alt: Preview of the pictogram sequence that will be downloaded as PDF
news.download-pdf.step2.description: The PDF contains exactly what you see in the preview: pictograms with the size, spacing and alignment you have set. You can share it by email or save it to your device.
news.download-pdf.summary: You can now download the sequence directly as a PDF file, without opening the print dialog.
news.download-pdf.title: Download sequence as PDF
news.logo-menu.content: Did you know the SequenciAAC logo is a button? Click it to open the main navigation menu, where you can access all pages and features of the application.
news.logo-menu.step1.alt: Menu navigation section with the Home, What's new, Edit and View links
news.logo-menu.step1.description: The first section of the menu holds the shortcuts to every page: Home, What's new (where you will find all the updates), Edit (to build your sequences) and View (to see and print them).
news.logo-menu.step2.alt: File section of the menu with Download and Load options
news.logo-menu.step2.description: From here you can manage your sequence files: Download saves the current sequence to a file on your device, and Load retrieves a previously saved sequence.
news.logo-menu.step3.alt: Settings section of the main menu
news.logo-menu.step3.description: Settings opens the preferences dialog, split into four tabs: User (the app language, the language pictograms are searched in, and the light or dark theme), Pictograms (typeface, frames and text position), View (page format) and Personal vocabulary.
news.logo-menu.summary: Click the logo to open the main menu and access all app features.
news.logo-menu.title: The navigation menu
news.multiple-sequences.content: Create as many sequences as you need! Use tabs to add new sequences or remove the ones you no longer need. Each sequence is independent and you can switch between them easily.
news.multiple-sequences.step1.alt: Sequence 1 with pictograms and button to add a new sequence
news.multiple-sequences.step1.descriptio: On the edit page, search for words in the search box (separated by commas) and pictograms will appear automatically in the active sequence. Click the + button to create a new sequence.
news.multiple-sequences.step2.alt: Two sequence tabs visible, sequence 2 active
news.multiple-sequences.step2.descriptio: Click any tab to switch to a different active sequence. Each sequence has its own independent content. Search for new words to fill sequence 2.
news.multiple-sequences.step3.alt: View of both sequences with size increased globally
news.multiple-sequences.step3.descriptio: In the View page, the "Apply to all" toggle lets you adjust the size and spacing of all sequences at once. Move the size control to see the change applied globally.
news.multiple-sequences.step4.alt: View with sequence 2 individually adjusted to a different size
news.multiple-sequences.step4.descriptio: Disable "Apply to all" to configure each sequence independently. Expand the accordion for the sequence you want to adjust and change its size or spacing without affecting the others.
news.multiple-sequences.summary: You can now create and manage multiple sequences at once with tabs.
news.multiple-sequences.title: Multiple sequences
news.new-languages.content:
SequenciAAC is now available in two new languages: Français (French) and Italiano (Italian). The application can now be used in five languages: Catalan, Spanish, English, French and Italian.

The translations have been done automatically, so there may be some inaccuracies or unnatural expressions. We apologise for any errors and we appreciate you letting us know so we can improve.
news.new-languages.step1.alt: Main menu open, showing the Settings entry
news.new-languages.step1.description: To change the language, open the main menu with the SequenciAAC logo and go into Settings. From the welcome screen you can also change it directly, with the language button in the header.
news.new-languages.step2.alt: Language section of the User tab, with all five languages visible
news.new-languages.step2.description: In the User tab, the «Interface» row shows all five languages —ca, en, es, fr and it—: tap the one you want and the whole app follows. Below it, «Search» picks the language pictograms are searched in, which can be a different one.
news.new-languages.step3.alt: The app with its interface in Français
news.new-languages.step3.description: The interface updates instantly. Here you can see the app in Français. If you find any incorrect translation, let us know: we will improve it.
news.new-languages.summary: The app speaks five languages. Here is where you change it.
news.new-languages.title: New languages: Français and Italiano
news.number-font.content: You can now configure the font of pictogram numbers independently. In the Default Settings dialog, enabling the Numbering switch reveals a new section to choose the font family, size, and color for the numbers, separately from the pictogram text font.
news.number-font.step1.alt: Default settings panel with the Numbering switch off
news.number-font.step1.description: Open the Default Settings dialog from the main menu (click the logo). You will see a switch to enable pictogram numbering.
news.number-font.step2.alt: Numbering switch enabled in the settings panel
news.number-font.step2.description: Enable the Numbering switch. Each pictogram will now show its order number on the opposite side of the text.
news.number-font.step3.alt: New number font section showing family, size and color selectors
news.number-font.step3.description: Once numbering is enabled, a new section appears to configure the number font: family, size, and color, independently from the pictogram text font.
news.number-font.summary: Choose an independent font for the numbers shown on pictograms.
news.number-font.title: Custom font for numbers
news.print-preview.content: The print preview shows you exactly how the printed page will look. You can control the pictogram size, row and column spacing, and alignment. Everything updates in real time!
news.print-preview.summary: Preview exactly how your page will look before printing.
news.print-preview.title: Print preview
news.save-improvements.content: The .saac file now saves the custom images you've uploaded, stored directly in the file so they're never lost. Additionally, the display settings for each sequence — pictogram size, spacing and alignment — are also saved and restored exactly as you left them.
news.save-improvements.step1.alt: Button to upload a custom image to the pictogram
news.save-improvements.step1.description: Upload your own image to any pictogram. The image is saved directly in the .saac file, without needing internet.
news.save-improvements.step2.alt: Save dialog with sequence and settings options
news.save-improvements.step2.description: When saving the file, all custom images are automatically included.
news.save-improvements.step3.description: The size, spacing and alignment of each sequence are automatically saved and restored when loading the file.
news.save-improvements.summary: The saved file now includes custom images and the size and spacing settings for each sequence.
news.save-improvements.title: Save improvements
news.save-load.content: You'll find the save and load options in the SequenciAAC logo menu. When saving, a file is downloaded with all sequences and pictogram images included. This way you can restore your work at any time!
news.save-load.summary: Download your sequences with images and load them whenever you want.
news.save-load.title: Save and restore
news.section.title: What's new
news.sequence-settings.content: You can now customize each sequence independently. Change the pictogram alignment (left, center or right), configure the number typography and color independently from the text, and discover more formatting options to adapt sequences to your needs.
news.sequence-settings.summary: Customize each sequence with alignment, number typography and more options.
news.sequence-settings.title: New per-sequence settings
news.view-improvements.content: Several bugs have been fixed that caused the print preview to not match the actual printed output. New controls have also been added for alignment and direction of sequences, and when you save a sequence the view settings are now automatically included.
news.view-improvements.step1.alt: Sequence preview showing exact match with printed output
news.view-improvements.step1.description: The sequence preview now corresponds exactly to the printed output. A precise scale calculation takes into account the page format (A4, A3) and screen resolution to faithfully show what will be printed.
news.view-improvements.step2.alt: Alignment and direction controls for sequences
news.view-improvements.step2.description: New controls to customize each sequence: choose the alignment (left, center, right) and direction (horizontal or vertical) to adapt the presentation to your needs.
news.view-improvements.step3.alt: Save sequence button with view settings included
news.view-improvements.step3.description: When you save the sequence using the download button, the view settings (sizes, spacing, alignment and direction) are automatically included in the file, so when you reload it everything will be as you left it.
news.view-improvements.summary: Print preview now matches output exactly. New alignment and direction controls.
news.view-improvements.title: Print preview improvements

news.autosave-draft.title: Your work is no longer lost
news.autosave-draft.summary: Your sequence saves itself as you work, and a new button tells you where it is.
news.autosave-draft.content: Until now, reloading the page or closing the tab by accident took hours of work with no warning. Your sequence now saves itself in this browser as you work, and a button at the bottom right tells you where your work is and how recent it is. It is a safety net, not a save: the browser can clear it, so real saving still means «Download» —the .saac file— and, with an account, the cloud.
news.autosave-draft.step1.alt: Editor with the round document status button at the bottom right
news.autosave-draft.step1.description: There is a new button at the bottom right. Its colour tells you at a glance how your work stands: green means it is where it should be, amber means you have a copy but it has fallen behind what is on screen.
news.autosave-draft.step2.alt: The status button open, showing the status sentence and the available actions
news.autosave-draft.step2.description: Press it and the full sentence appears —«Only on this device, since…»— along with the actions: save, download the file, and start a new document, which previously was not possible without reloading.
news.pictogram-actions-touch.title: Pictogram actions, on tablets too
news.pictogram-actions-touch.summary: Copy, paste, insert and duplicate no longer depend on right-click.
news.pictogram-actions-touch.content: These actions only opened with a right-click, and on iPad and iPhone that menu never opens. Edit and delete were still reachable through the pictogram dialog, but copy, paste, insert and duplicate had no door at all — precisely the four you use to build the sequence. They are now in that dialog's menu too, the same on computer and tablet. Along the way, the menu is no longer in English and the labels say what they actually do.
news.pictogram-actions-touch.step1.alt: Pictogram edit dialog with the more-actions button in the header
news.pictogram-actions-touch.step1.descr: Tap a pictogram to open its edit dialog. The more-actions button is in the top right corner.
news.pictogram-actions-touch.step2.alt: Expanded menu with the four pictogram-building actions
news.pictogram-actions-touch.step2.descr: All four appear: copy, paste —which replaces the pictogram, and now says so—, insert an empty one after it, and duplicate after it. Deleting it is still the button in the dialog footer.
news.search-suggestions.title: Type the phrase and find the pictograms
news.search-suggestions.summary: The search box suggests words as you type, and a whole phrase becomes a sequence.
news.search-suggestions.content: As you type, the search box proposes words and you can accept them with the Tab key. And you no longer need to look them up one by one: type the whole phrase, separated by commas, and the app builds the sequence word by word, with a bar showing how far along it is.
news.search-suggestions.step1.alt: Search box with the suggestion list open and the «Tab» chip
news.search-suggestions.step1.descriptio: Start typing and the suggestions appear. The «Tab» chip reminds you that the Tab key accepts the highlighted word, so you do not have to type it in full.
news.search-suggestions.step2.alt: Sequence with three pictograms produced from a single phrase
news.search-suggestions.step2.descriptio: Type the whole phrase separated by commas and press Enter: each word becomes a pictogram in the sequence, in the order you wrote it.
news.user-preferences.title: Dark theme and expanded settings
news.user-preferences.summary: The app now has a dark mode, and the settings are split into tabs.
news.user-preferences.content: The settings dialog is now split into tabs, and one of them is new and about you: under User you will find the app language, the language pictograms are searched in, and the theme, light or dark. The preview sheet stays white in dark mode too, and that is deliberate: what you see on screen is what will come out printed.
news.user-preferences.step1.alt: User tab of the settings with the theme selector
news.user-preferences.step1.description: Open Settings from the main menu. The theme selector is in the User tab: light, dark, or whatever the system says.
news.user-preferences.step2.alt: The editor in dark theme, with the sequence sheet still white
news.user-preferences.step2.description: The whole interface goes dark, but the sheet stays white: it is what gets printed, and the contrast of text on paper has to be judged while you are setting it up.
news.pdf-quality.title: The PDF comes out as you see it
news.pdf-quality.summary: The PDF no longer loses quality depending on how small the preview looks.
news.pdf-quality.content: The PDF was generated at the resolution the preview happened to be shown at: the smaller the screen, the worse the file — precisely the worst case for anyone exporting from a tablet. It now always comes out at the right resolution, the image is centred on the page instead of pushing all the margin to one side, and no blank sheet can come out any more. While it is being generated, the app tells you what it is doing.
news.pdf-quality.step1.alt: Sequence preview on the view page
news.pdf-quality.step1.description: What you see in the preview is what you will find in the PDF: the same size, the same spacing and the same margins, whether you are looking at a big screen or a small one.
news.pdf-quality.step2.alt: Waiting message while the PDF is generated
news.pdf-quality.step2.description: When you press the PDF button, the app says it is generating it, and tells you both when it finishes and if something fails. Before, the only signal was the button turning grey.
news.safe-delete.title: No sequence is deleted without warning
news.safe-delete.summary: Deleting a sequence now asks first, and says how many pictograms will go.
news.safe-delete.content: The app has no undo, so deleting a whole sequence was the easiest way to lose work: it took all its pictograms with it and asked nothing. Now it asks, and gives the number. If the sequence is empty it does not ask: there is no point requesting permission to throw away blank slots. And in the pictogram menu, «Delete» has moved out of the middle and gone to the very end, on its own.
news.safe-delete.step1.alt: Confirmation dialog stating how many pictograms will be deleted

news.documents-everywhere.title: SequenciAAC documents now look the same everywhere
news.documents-everywhere.summary: A .saac file opens and prints the same on any computer, tablet or phone. Saving is simpler, and the style can be reused.
news.documents-everywhere.content:
This October we are launching a new way of saving SequenciAAC documents. A .saac file now opens and prints the same on any computer, tablet or phone. Saving is simpler, and the style can be reused in other documents.

Until now, when saving you had to choose between «Sequence» and «Default settings». If the right option wasn't ticked, the document opened on another computer with a different font, different borders or a different page size. We have fixed this at the root. It is not a patch: we have changed how documents are saved on the inside, so that the ones you make today keep working for many years to come.
news.documents-everywhere.step1.title: A single «Save document» button
news.documents-everywhere.step1.descript:
You no longer have to choose what gets saved. The Save document button saves the whole document in a .saac file.

What a document saves

  • All the sequences in the document, each with its pictograms and in the same order.
  • How each card looks: the font, the size, the colours, the borders, the numbering and the position of the text.
  • The changes you have made to a single pictogram, such as a border in another colour or a crossed-out pictogram.
  • The size of the pictograms, the space between them and the alignment of each sequence.
  • The page: the size, the orientation and whether the sequences go in rows or in columns.
  • Your own images, inside the same file. If you use the same photo several times, it is only saved once.

What is not saved: your app preferences, such as the language or the default style for new documents. That is why opening someone else's document never changes your settings.
news.documents-everywhere.step2.title: Your style, reusable
news.documents-everywhere.step2.descript:
If you have found a style that works, such as the school font, borders in the classroom colour or large numbering, you can now save it in a style file (.saacstyle) and apply it to any document.

Style files can also be shared. A teaching team can use the same style and all the school materials will look the same.

If you open a style file from «Load», the app recognises it and asks you what you want to do with it.
news.documents-everywhere.step3.title: The general style and changes to a single pictogram
news.documents-everywhere.step3.descript:
Each document has a general style, which is the one all the cards share. If you change something in a single pictogram, only that change is saved, and the rest follows the general style.

An example: the document uses blue borders, and you make the border of the «breakfast» pictogram red so that it stands out. If you then change the font of the whole document, «breakfast» changes font too, but keeps its red border.

So that you always know what is going on:

  • When you edit a pictogram with its own changes, the Reset button appears next to Pictogram style, to make it follow the general style again.
  • In the grid, customised pictograms have a small mark in the corner. Only you see it while you edit: it never appears in the printout, the PDF or full screen.
  • You can also reset them from the pictogram menu, with Reset style.
  • Apply All gives all the cards the same style and removes their own changes.
  • If you make a mistake, Undo puts it back the way it was.
news.documents-everywhere.step4.title: Your old documents and your phone
news.documents-everywhere.step4.descript:
Old documents keep working. When you open one, the app adapts it by itself and lets you know. The original file is not touched: when you save it again, it will be saved the new way.

  • If the old document had no style of its own, your default style is applied and we tell you so.
  • Empty tabs, without any pictogram, are removed.
  • Each card still looks the same as before.

On your phone, the file downloads with the right name. Before, on Android and iPhone the file could end up as «routine.saac.txt». Now it downloads as «routine.saac». Files you already have with «.txt» at the end also open without having to rename them.
news.documents-everywhere.step5.title: How a document is designed
news.documents-everywhere.step5.descript:
From now on, everything new in SequenciAAC will follow these six ideas.

  1. The document carries everything. The sequences, how they look, the page and your photos go inside the same file. That is why it looks the same everywhere, with or without an account.
  2. Document, sequences and pictograms. A document has several sequences, the ones you see as tabs, and each sequence has its pictograms.
  3. One general style, and each pictogram's changes kept apart. The document has the general style. Each sequence can have its own size, space between pictograms and alignment. Each pictogram only remembers what you have changed in it. That way, changing the look of the whole document is easy, and no card ends up different without you knowing.
  4. What is yours stays with you. The app language and your preferences do not travel with the document.
  5. One file, one thing. A .saac is a document, and a .saacstyle is a style. The app knows what each file is even if your phone has changed its name.
  6. Ready for the future. When SequenciAAC improves, your documents will keep opening and will adapt by themselves, as old ones do now, without you losing anything. If one day you open a document made with a newer version of the app, it will warn you first.
news.documents-everywhere.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
news.documents-everywhere.faq.q1: Do I have to do anything with my files?
news.documents-everywhere.faq.a1: No. Open them as always. If you want them saved the new way, save them again.
news.documents-everywhere.faq.q2: What is the difference between a .saac and a .saacstyle?
news.documents-everywhere.faq.a2: A .saac is a document with its sequences. A .saacstyle is only a style, to apply to other documents.
news.documents-everywhere.faq.q3: If I send a document to another family or to the school, will they see it the same?
news.documents-everywhere.faq.a3: Yes. The document carries the font, the borders, the sizes, the page and your own images.
news.documents-everywhere.faq.q4: Will opening someone else's document change my settings?
news.documents-everywhere.faq.a4: No. Your preferences only change if you choose to.
news.documents-everywhere.faq.q5: Will the «customised» mark appear when I print?
news.documents-everywhere.faq.a5: No. You only see it while you edit.
news.documents-everywhere.closing: SequenciAAC is still free and works without an account. If you run into any problem with your documents, tell us about it.

news.edit-text-on-card.title: Change a pictogram's text without leaving the grid
news.edit-text-on-card.summary: Click the word under the pictogram and type another one: no window to open anymore.
news.edit-text-on-card.content: Until now, changing the word that goes with a pictogram meant opening its edit window, finding the text and closing it again. Now you type it straight onto the card, in the same grid where you build the sequence.
news.edit-text-on-card.step1.description:
Click the word on the card and it turns into a field you can type in, with the text already selected. Type a new one.

To save it, press Enter or click anywhere else. If you change your mind, Esc leaves everything as it was.
news.edit-text-on-card.step1.alt: A sequence of pictograms: the word of the second one is being rewritten on the card itself
news.edit-text-on-card.step2.description: The card now shows the new text. If you ever delete all the text and leave it empty, the card goes back to the word you searched for.
news.edit-text-on-card.step2.alt: The same sequence with the new text saved under the second pictogram
news.edit-text-on-card.step3.description:
You can also get there other ways:

  • Right-click the pictogram and choose “Edit text”.
  • With the keyboard: move to the card and press F2.
news.edit-text-on-card.step3.alt: A pictogram's right-click menu, with the “Edit text” option highlighted
news.edit-text-on-card.closing: Clicking the pictogram's image still opens the edit window, with all the usual settings. And if the card shows no text, you change the word from there, with “Edit”.
